title: Angular binding
description:
How one agnostic component contract is realised in Angular. The reasoning is in packages/contracts/README.md.

This is the SMALLEST of the three binding schemas, and the reason is structural rather than incidental: in Angular a component does not render its own root element, it ATTACHES to one. `element` therefore compiles into the component's SELECTOR — `button[dsSwitch]` — and everything React records about what happens to that root (where a ref lands, where a className merges) is either automatic or does not apply.

Keep it SMALL. If a field here would be equally true in React or Vue, it belongs in `@ds/platform-web` or in the contract instead.

component.description: Must match the contract's `component`, the directory name, and the exported class.

contract.description: Relative path to the agnostic contract this realises.

framework.description: Named explicitly so a directory can hold more than one binding without ambiguity.

element.description:
The element the component attaches to — what the contract's `semantics.role` becomes in the DOM.

IT BECOMES THE SELECTOR, not markup: `element: "button"` for `Switch` compiles to `selector: 'button[dsSwitch]'`, and a consumer writes `<button dsSwitch>`. This is the one structural fact that differs in KIND from the React and Vue backends rather than in spelling, and it is why this schema has no `elementByProp`: an Angular selector is static, so a root element that changes with a prop cannot be expressed at all. The emitter refuses such a contract rather than rendering a wrapper element and pretending.

IDENTICAL to the React and Vue bindings' `element` in all fifteen components, because which element carries a role is web-platform knowledge. `pnpm verify:parity` fails when the three disagree.

propOverrides.description: Where a contract axis is exposed under a different input name in Angular, because the framework already owns the canonical one. Keyed by axis name.

reason.description: Required. A rename with no reason is drift with paperwork.
